summary: Target-driven cleanup that reclaims disk until a free-space goal is met

delivery.outcome: fixos cleanup --free-gb N (alias --target-free-gb) reclaims disk space in a bounded ladder of no-privilege tiers - safe service caches, stale /tmp entries, stale agent release caches under ~/.local/share/*/releases older than 7 days, Docker dangling images and build cache, and Docker images unreferenced by any container and older than --days - stopping as soon as statvfs free space reaches the goal. Every Docker call runs with a hard timeout so a busy daemon skips its tier instead of hanging, non-writable (protected) release directories are skipped, and when the goal is still unmet the command prints the exact privileged next steps (old snap revisions, rotated syslog) instead of failing silently. --threshold-gb keeps its per-service scan meaning and its help text now says it is not a free-space goal.
nonGoals: No deletion of user documents, Ollama models, editor extensions, Docker volumes or any path requiring elevated privileges
No change to existing sub-action flags or their semantics
No scheduler/daemon: the ladder runs only when explicitly requested

architecture.decision: Add fixos/cli/_cleanup_free_target.py with pure helpers (statvfs free bytes, stale release-cache discovery by mtime with protected-path skipping, batched docker subprocess calls with timeouts) and a generic ladder runner that measures free space before and after each tier and stops at the goal. cleanup_cmd.py gains --free-gb/--target-free-gb which must run as a standalone action (same guard pattern as --venvs-old) and composes existing handlers (safe plan via --yes executor, _cleanup_tmp for stale temp) with the new tiers. Unit tests mock df and docker so the ladder logic is verified without touching a real system.
interfaceChanges: New cleanup options --free-gb/--target-free-gb (standalone action, implies the safe --yes pass first)
architecture.rollback: Revert the commit; cleanup keeps only the pre-existing per-service and sub-action modes.
